entities.summary: Denmark is a Nordic country in Northern Europe. It is the metropole and most populous constituent of the Kingdom of Denmark, also known as the Danish Realm, a constitutionally unitary state that includes the autonomous territories of the Faroe Islands and Greenland in the north Atlantic Ocean. Metropolitan Denmark, also called "continental Denmark" or "Denmark proper", consists of the northern Jutland peninsula and an archipelago of 406 islands. It is the southernmost of the Scandinavian countries, lying southwest of Sweden, south of Norway, and north of Germany, with which it shares a short border.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Denmark played a significant role in the Hanseatic League, a powerful mercantile and cultural organization that dominated trade in Northern Europe from the 13th to the 16th century. The country's strategic location allowed it to control key trade routes between Europe and Asia.
